strings_1.title: What is a String?
strings_1.explanation: String is the name we give to texts in programming! "Hello, world!" is a string. It is always enclosed in quotes!

strings_2.title: Joining Strings
strings_2.prompt: We can use + to join two strings. True or false? ➕
strings_2.explanation: Yes! "Hello, " + "world!" makes "Hello, world!". It's like gluing two pieces of paper together!

strings_3.title: Uppercase
strings_3.prompt: Complete the code to transform the text to uppercase: 🔠
strings_3.explanation: The upper() method transforms all letters to UPPERCASE! It's like shouting the text! 📢

strings_4.title: String Length
strings_4.prompt: Which function do we use to find out how many letters are in a string? 📏
strings_4.explanation: The len() function counts how many characters are in the string. len("Python") gives 6, because Python has 6 letters!

strings_5.title: Counting Vowels
strings_5.prompt: Create a function that counts how many vowels (a, e, i, o, u) are in a word: 🔤
strings_5.explanation: Go through each letter of the text with a for loop. If the letter is in the list of vowels, add 1 to the counter!

strings_6.title: Magic F-string
strings_6.prompt: Use an f-string to put the age in the text:
strings_6.explanation: By putting an f before the quotes, you can use {variable} inside the text! Python changes {nome} to "Leo" automatically. ✨

strings_split_1.title: Breaking the Text
strings_split_1.explanation: split() breaks the text at the spaces and returns a list! Each word becomes a separate item. ✂️

strings_split_2.title: Separating by Comma
strings_split_2.explanation: You can tell it where to cut! split(",") cuts at the commas. Each piece becomes a list item! 🍎

strings_join_1.title: Joining the List
strings_join_1.explanation: join() is the opposite of split! It joins the list items using the text before the dot as glue! 🧲

strings_join_2.title: Joining with Space
strings_join_2.prompt: Complete to join the words with a space:
strings_join_2.explanation: " ".join(lista) uses space as glue between words! Result: "I love Python". 📝

strings_7.title: First Letters
strings_7.prompt: Complete to get the first 3 letters of "Python":
strings_7.explanation: We use [0:3] to get from the beginning (0) until before 3. P(0), y(1), t(2). The h(3) is left out! ✂️

strings_8.title: Magic Sentence
strings_8.prompt: Use f-string to put the age in the text:
strings_8.explanation: F-string is magic! Just put the variable inside curly braces { } and Python swaps it for the value. Don't forget the f before the quotes! 🎩

strings_lower.title: Lowercase Text
strings_lower.prompt: If upper() shouts, lower() whispers! Complete to make the text lowercase:
strings_lower.explanation: lower() transforms everything into small (lowercase) letters. Great for when we don't want to shout! 🤫

strings_replace.title: Swapping Words
strings_replace.explanation: replace("old", "new") looks for the old word and swaps it for the new one! It's like editing text automatically. 🔄

strings_strip.title: Cleaning Spaces
strings_strip.prompt: What does the strip() method do?
strings_strip.explanation: strip() cleans up the mess! It removes empty spaces that are left over at the beginning and end of the text. ✨
options: Removes spaces from beginning and end
Removes letters s, t, r, i, p

strings_9.title: Cutting the Middle
strings_9.prompt: Get the letters "yth" from the word "Python":
strings_9.explanation: We want from index 1 ("y") to 3 ("h"). But slicing stops BEFORE the end, so we use [1:4]! 🍰

strings_10.title: Double F-string
strings_10.prompt: Complete the f-string with name and age:
strings_10.explanation: You can put as many variables as you want in an f-string! Just use curly braces {} for each one. Double magic! ✨✨

strings_11.title: Pretty Title
strings_11.prompt: The `.title()` method makes the first letter of each word uppercase.
strings_11.explanation: Yes! `title()` makes the text fancy! "the mouse gnawed" becomes "The Mouse Gnawed". Great for names and titles! 🎩

strings_12.title: The Last Letter
strings_12.prompt: Use a negative index to get the last letter of the word:
strings_12.explanation: Negative indices count backwards! -1 is the last item, -2 is the second to last... It's a super useful shortcut! 🔙

strings_13.title: Separating Dates
strings_13.prompt: Separate the day, month, and year by cutting at the slashes (/):
strings_13.explanation: split("/") cuts the text wherever there is a slash! This is how we separate the date parts. 📅

strings_14.title: Word Train
strings_14.prompt: Join the list `["choo", "choo"]` with "-" to make a train:
strings_14.explanation: `join` is the glue! It uses the dash "-" to glue the wagons and become "choo-choo". All aboard! 🚂

strings_15.title: Counting Letters
strings_15.prompt: Use `count()` to count how many times the letter "a" appears in the word:
strings_15.explanation: `count()` counts how many times something appears in the text. In "banana", the letter "a" appears 3 times! 🔢

strings_16.title: Game Scoreboard
strings_16.prompt: Use f-string to show the name and points:
strings_16.explanation: With an f-string, you can quickly build complex sentences! Just put the variables in the right places inside the braces { }. 🏆

boss_battle_8.title: The Mysterious Scribe
boss_battle_8.prompt: The Scribe wrote "python" in lowercase. Transform it to UPPERCASE and show it!
boss_battle_8.explanation: The Scribe wants you to shout! Use upper() to make everything uppercase! 📜
